raised: Once you scroll, the company name disappears, so you can't tell which company a row (e.g. fund 8211) belongs to
The page doesn't show what the fees would actually cost in shekels
The fees are from 2025 but the other figures are from September 2026, with no reason given
The legend's 'הזנתה' and the line and box styles are not understood
The orange 'not updated' warning is unsettling and seems to clash with the 03.11.2026 date at the bottom
It wasn't clear that the filter buttons could narrow the table to the 'כללי' tracks
The 'קיימי' filter is not understood
The two government-bond filters look like the same thing
The table is very long and tiring to scroll
The new Ayalon tracks are empty or not reported, some showing 0 million ₪
The note saying returns are before fees and not a forecast comes too late, at the very bottom
The 'מההפקדות' fee is almost always 0%, and 'עוד לא דווח' lowered confidence
The donut circles add nothing beyond the numbers
The foreign-currency (מט"ח) exposure number is not understood, e.g. what 99% means
'מניות 101%': unclear how more than 100% can be in shares
Unclear why the same S&P 500 index has different fees at different companies
Returns are shown before fees, so the reader must subtract the fee themselves
Unclear whether the fee can be negotiated or whether the average is what they would pay
No worst-year or possible-loss information for each track
No information on withdrawal at 60+, tax, or turning the money into a monthly pension
No guidance on how to actually open a fund, and no contact details
No simple guidance for someone near retirement
The 'קופה' fund-number column could be dropped
The second row of filter buttons could be dropped

problems.why: The reader says they did not understand the foreign-currency figure in the exposure column, and later also asks how shares can be 101%. Together that matches the complaint that the column is unexplained and shows values above 100%.

raised: Once you scroll, the company name disappears, so you can't tell which company a row (e.g. fund 8211) belongs to
The page doesn't say what you would actually pay, or what the numbers mean in shekels
The fee is a 2025 average while the other figures are from September 2026, and it isn't clear why
The legend is confusing: 'הזנתה' is unknown, and the dotted/solid/blue markers can't be matched to the table
The orange warning about data not updated since September 2026 is unsettling and seems to clash with the 03.11.2026 date at the bottom
It wasn't clear that the filter buttons (e.g. 'כללי 12') could be pressed to show only those tracks
'קיימי' in the filter buttons isn't understood
'אג"ח ממשלתי סחיר' and 'אג"ח ממשלות' look like the same thing
The table is very long, and scrolling through about fifteen screens is tiring
The new Ayalon tracks marked 'חדש'/'עוד לא דווח' (some at 0 million ₪) show nothing useful and clutter the table
The note saying returns are before fees and not a forecast sits at the bottom, too late, and should come first
The 'מההפקדות' fee line is almost always 0%, so it isn't useful, and 'עוד לא דווח' there lowers confidence in that company
The donut circles add nothing beyond the numbers
The foreign-currency (מט"ח) exposure number isn't understood: is 99% good or dangerous?
'מניות 101%': how can more than 100% be in shares?
It's unclear why the same S&P 500 index track costs 0.54% at one company and 0.71% at another
Returns are shown before fees, so you have to work out the after-fee return yourself
It's unclear whether the average fee is what you would pay or whether it can be negotiated
There's no information on possible losses or the worst year (e.g. 2022)
There's no information on withdrawals at 60+, tax, or turning the savings into a monthly pension
There's no contact information or next step for actually opening a fund
There's no simple guidance on which tracks suit someone near retirement
The 'קופה' fund-number column is unnecessary in the main table
The second row of filter buttons is unnecessary

problems.why: The reader asks directly how 'מניות 101%' can mean more than 100% in shares. That is the person's complaint that the exposure column shows figures above 100% with no explanation (item 14, on not understanding the foreign-currency figure, also overlaps).
